summary: Acute cutaneous laceration or open wound disrupting epidermal and dermal barrier. Direct pressure and sterile cleansing required.
source: WHO ICD-11 & Advanced Trauma Life Support (ATLS) Guidelines

questions.prompt: Is the bleeding controlled with direct pressure, or is it bleeding continuously or spurting?
Do you feel numbness or loss of sensation beyond the cut, or difficulty moving the joint/finger?
Have you received a Tetanus toxoid booster vaccine within the past 5 to 10 years?

safeMeasures: Wash wound thoroughly under clean running tap water for 3 to 5 minutes with mild soap
Apply continuous direct pressure using a clean sterile gauze or cloth to arrest bleeding
Apply topical antiseptic ointment (Neosporin or Bacitracin) and cover with a sterile bandage
Keep the affected limb elevated above heart level to minimize swelling and throbbing

suggestedOtc.indication: Topical antimicrobial for clean minor cuts and abrasions
suggestedOtc.dosage: Apply thin film to clean wound 1 to 2 times daily
suggestedOtc.contraindications: Deep puncture wounds or animal bites requiring systemic antibiotics

suggestedOtc.indication: Oral analgesic for mild-to-moderate wound pain
suggestedOtc.dosage: 1 tablet every 6 to 8 hours as needed (do not exceed 3000mg/day)

redFlags: Continuous bleeding that does not stop after 10 minutes of direct firm pressure
Pulsating or spurting bright red arterial bleeding
Deep wound gaping open more than 1/4 inch requiring surgical sutures
Loss of sensation, tingling, or inability to flex or extend the finger/joint
Wound caused by rusty metal, soil contamination, or animal/human bite

summary: Thermal injury to dermal tissue from contact with hot liquids, steam, surfaces, or flames. Immediate cooling and barrier protection essential.
source: WHO ICD-11 & International Society for Burn Injuries (ISBI) Protocols

questions.prompt: What does the burn look like (red without blisters, blistering with fluid, or charred/white/numb)?
replies: Skin is white, charred, or numb

questions.prompt: How large is the burned area compared to the size of the patient's palm?

safeMeasures: Immediately cool the burn under cool (not ice-cold) running tap water for 15 to 20 minutes
Do NOT apply ice, butter, toothpaste, or greasy ointments to fresh burns
Do NOT deliberately pop or puncture intact blisters
Cover loosely with sterile non-adherent dressing or clean plastic cling wrap

suggestedOtc.saltName: Silver Sulfadiazine 1% Cream / Aloe Vera Gel
suggestedOtc.indication: Soothing antimicrobial barrier for superficial second-degree burns
suggestedOtc.dosage: Apply thin layer to cooled, clean burn 1-2 times daily
suggestedOtc.contraindications: Sulfa drug allergy; do not use on face near eyes

redFlags: Burn larger than palm size or involving face, hands, feet, groin, or major joints
Third-degree burns: white, leathery, charred, or completely painless skin
Chemical or high-voltage electrical burns
Signs of infection: spreading erythema, foul-smelling pus, or fever

summary: Traumatic stretching or microscopic tearing of joint ligaments following inversion, twisting, or mechanical overload.
source: WHO ICD-11 & Ottawa Ankle/Knee Clinical Rules

questions.prompt: Can you put weight on the limb and take 4 steps, or is it completely impossible to bear weight?
replies: Painful but can walk a few steps

questions.prompt: Is there visible bony deformity, severe bruising, or rapid massive swelling within 30 minutes?

safeMeasures: Follow R.I.C.E. protocol: Rest the joint and avoid strenuous loading
Ice: Apply ice wrapped in a damp cloth for 15 minutes every 2 to 3 hours
Compression: Wrap with an elastic compression bandage (not overly tight)
Elevation: Elevate the joint above heart level to assist venous lymphatic drainage

suggestedOtc.dosage: Gently massage 2-4g onto affected joint 3 to 4 times daily

suggestedOtc.contraindications: Active peptic ulcer disease, severe renal insufficiency

redFlags: Visible bone deformity, angulation, or open skin over the injured joint
Inability to bear any weight immediately after injury and take 4 steps (Ottawa criteria)
Intense focal bone tenderness on the posterior edge of malleolus or navicular bone
Coldness, pale discoloration, or loss of distal pulse in foot/hand

summary: Acute dental pain arising from bacterial caries, pulpal inflammation, or periodontal abscess.
source: WHO ICD-11 & American Dental Association (ADA) Clinical Guidelines

questions.prompt: Is the pain triggered by hot or cold fluids, or is it a continuous throbbing pain that keeps you awake?
Do you notice facial swelling, difficulty opening your mouth (trismus), or high fever?

safeMeasures: Rinse mouth gently with warm salt water (1/2 tsp salt in warm water) every 3-4 hours
Floss carefully around the tooth to dislodge any trapped food particles
Do NOT place aspirin or analgesic tablets directly against the gum tissue (causes chemical burn)
Sleep with head elevated on pillows to reduce intracranial blood pressure to the tooth

suggestedOtc.indication: Gold-standard synergy for acute odontogenic inflammation
suggestedOtc.contraindications: Peptic ulcer disease or severe liver disorder

suggestedOtc.indication: Topical numbing and antimicrobial dental rinse
suggestedOtc.dosage: Dab clove oil with cotton tip on tooth cavity; rinse chlorhexidine 2x daily

redFlags: Facial cellulitis or rapid swelling spreading under the jaw, floor of mouth, or towards eye
Difficulty swallowing saliva, drooling, or difficulty breathing (Ludwig angina risk)
High fever, chills, or difficulty opening mouth wider than two fingers (trismus)

summary: Fever in pediatric populations. In infants under 3 months, fever represents a medical emergency requiring sepsis evaluation.
source: WHO Integrated Management of Childhood Illness (IMCI) & AAP Guidelines

questions.prompt: How old is the child or infant, and what is the rectal/axillary temperature reading?
Is the child drinking fluids, making wet diapers, and alert, or are they unusually lethargic or floppy?

safeMeasures: Dress the child in lightweight single-layer clothing; avoid heavy bundling
Offer frequent breast milk, formula, or oral rehydration fluids to prevent dehydration
Keep room comfortably ventilated around 20-22°C (68-72°F)

suggestedOtc.indication: Antipyretic for infants over 3 months of age
suggestedOtc.dosage: 10-15 mg/kg per dose every 4-6 hours (strictly verified by infant weight)
suggestedOtc.contraindications: Do NOT give to infants under 3 months without physician examination; NEVER give Aspirin to children

redFlags: Any infant under 3 months of age with a temperature of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher (immediate ER)
Lethargy, limpness, unresponsive, or bulging soft spot (fontanelle) on scalp
Purplish non-blanching pinprick rash (petechiae) anywhere on body
Stridor, grunting breathing, or blue discoloration around lips

summary: Lower urinary tract mucosal infection typically caused by uropathogenic E. coli, causing burning micturition, frequency, and pelvic heaviness.
source: WHO ICD-11 & EAU Guidelines on Urological Infections

questions.prompt: Are you having burning or pain during urination, increased frequency or urgency, or any lower pelvic pain?
How long have these symptoms been present, and when did they first start?

safeMeasures: Drink 3 to 4 liters of clean water daily to flush urinary bacterial colonizations
Avoid bladder irritants including caffeine, alcohol, artificial sweeteners, and hot spicy foods
Urinate frequently without holding urine; wipe front to back

suggestedOtc.saltName: Potassium Citrate Liquid / Disodium Hydrogen Citrate
suggestedOtc.indication: Systemic urine alkalizer to alleviate painful burning micturition
suggestedOtc.dosage: 15ml diluted in a full glass of water 3 times daily after meals

redFlags: High spiking fever with shaking chills or rigors
Unilateral or bilateral flank / lower back pain (costovertebral angle tenderness indicating pyelonephritis)
Visible red blood in urine (gross hematuria)
Persistent nausea and vomiting with inability to keep fluids

summary: Ocular conjunctival irritation, vascular hyperemia, and ciliary muscle fatigue from prolonged digital display exposure or contact allergens.
source: WHO ICD-11 & American Academy of Ophthalmology (AAO) Guidelines

questions.prompt: Are you experiencing eye redness, itching, watery discharge, or noticeable blurriness and visual strain?

safeMeasures: Practice 20-20-20 screen rule: Every 20 minutes, look at an object 20 feet away for 20 seconds
Apply cool sterile saline compress over closed eyelids for 10 minutes to soothe vascular congestion
Discontinue contact lens use until all irritation and redness completely resolve
Avoid rubbing eyes to prevent mechanical micro-abrasions to corneal epithelium

suggestedOtc.indication: Preservative-free artificial tear lubricant for ocular fatigue and irritation
suggestedOtc.dosage: Instill 1 to 2 drops in affected eye(s) 3 to 4 times daily as needed
suggestedOtc.contraindications: Do not touch dropper tip directly to eyeball or eyelid surface

redFlags: Sudden loss or severe reduction in visual acuity
Severe deep ocular pain, halo rings around lights, or nausea (acute angle-closure glaucoma)
Copious thick green/yellow purulent discharge gluing eyelids shut in morning (bacterial conjunctivitis)
History of chemical splash or foreign body penetrating the eye

summary: Gastric mucosal inflammation caused by hyperacidity, H. pylori, NSAID irritation, or dietary indiscretion.
source: WHO ICD-11 & American College of Gastroenterology (ACG) Guidelines

questions.prompt: Where is the abdominal discomfort located (upper stomach, lower abdomen, or all over), and does it come in waves or stay constant?

safeMeasures: Adopt a bland BRAT diet (bananas, white rice, applesauce, toast, oatmeal)
Sip warm water or ginger tea; stay upright for 45 minutes after eating
Strictly avoid deep-fried, oily meals, chili peppers, coffee, alcohol, and NSAID painkillers

suggestedOtc.indication: Neutralizes gastric acid hypersecretion and relieves bloating gas
suggestedOtc.dosage: 10ml gel or 1 tablet 30 minutes before meals or at bedtime

redFlags: Rigid board-like abdomen or severe rebound tenderness (peritonitis / perforation)
Black tarry stools (melena) or vomiting blood / coffee-ground emesis
Severe right lower quadrant pain with fever (appendicitis concern)

condition: Primary Headache Disorder / Migraine / Tension Cephalea
summary: Benign primary cephalea presenting as unilateral throbbing neurovascular pain or bilateral band-like tension pressure.
source: WHO ICD-11 & International Headache Society (IHS) Classification (ICHD-3)

questions.prompt: How would you describe the headache (throbbing, dull pressure, or sharp), and does light or sound make it worse?

safeMeasures: Rest quietly in a darkened, noise-isolated room with eyes closed
Apply a cool damp cloth or ice pack wrapped in a towel over forehead or temples
Hydrate with oral electrolytes and avoid skipping meals

suggestedOtc.indication: Acute analgesia for tension headache or early-phase migraine
suggestedOtc.dosage: 1 tablet at onset of headache with water (do not exceed daily safe limits)

redFlags: Sudden explosive thunderclap headache reaching maximum intensity in seconds
Headache with stiff neck, photophobia, and high fever (meningitis concern)
New focal neurological deficit: slurred speech, facial drooping, or one-sided limb weakness

summary: Acute viral inflammatory reaction of bronchial mucosa resulting in cough with or without sputum production.
source: WHO ICD-11 & Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD)

questions.prompt: Is your cough dry, or is it producing phlegm or mucus?

safeMeasures: Inhale warm steam for 10 minutes 2 to 3 times daily to loosen tracheobronchial secretions
Drink warm water, honey, and lemon tea to coat and soothe hypersensitive pharynx
Avoid exposure to tobacco smoke, dust, and cold ambient air

suggestedOtc.indication: Mucolytic expectorant that thins thick bronchial mucus for easier clearance
suggestedOtc.dosage: 10ml syrup 3 times daily with a full glass of water
suggestedOtc.contraindications: Do not combine with cough suppressants; drink ample water

suggestedOtc.indication: Centrally acting cough suppressant for non-productive hacking cough
suggestedOtc.dosage: 10ml syrup every 6 to 8 hours as needed

redFlags: Coughing up frank blood or rust-colored sputum (hemoptysis)
Severe shortness of breath, audible wheezing, or chest retraction while breathing
High persistent fever > 102°F lasting more than 3 days with chest pain
